(a) the discrimination of formal relations is a functional-analytic phenomenon, (b) the discrimination of a physical relation (e.g., color) is a functional-analyzed phenomenon, (c) the discrimination of physical relations is a functional analytic phenomenon, and (d) the discrimination of functional relations is a functional analysis phenomenon.
we have demonstrated a functional-analytic account of analogical reasoning.
we trained and tested human adults for equivalence-equivalence relations, and then tested them for the discrimination of physical similarity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a model of analogical thinking based on relational frame analysis.
the development of a functional-analytic account of analogical reasoning that may provide the basis for a new model of the cognitive sciences.
the analysis and experimental manipulation of analogical reasoning in adult humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model of analogy described here is a viable model for the discrimination of a formal similarity between relations.
relational frame theory (RFT), a behavior-analytically oriented account of language and cognition, provides a model of the psychological processes underlying the analogical reasoning.
the present study has shown that equivalence-equivalence relations can be established in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the basic model of analogy is a functional-analytic one that can explain the transformation of functions of stimuli in the context of analogical reasoning.
we have shown that a behavior-analytically defined model of analogy, in which equivalence-equivalence responding allows the discrimination of formal similarities, can be demonstrated in humans.
the relational frame theory of language is a functional-analytic theory that can be tested experimentally and that it can be applied in clinical settings to understand and treat human behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relational frame model of analogical transfer is an empirically viable model of analogy.
the relational frame model of analogy provides an account of the emergence of analogy as a product of equivalence relations and equivalence-equivalence relations.
the relational frame model of analogy can be applied to the analysis of human behavior.
